sections.title: Duties
paragraphs: A keeper lit the lamp at sunset.
A keeper trimmed the wick every four hours.
A keeper polished the lens each morning.
A keeper wrote the weather in the log.
A keeper painted the tower every spring.
A keeper rang the fog bell when the fog came in from the sea.

sections.title: Equipment
paragraphs: The lamp burned whale oil until 1860, then paraffin, and finally electricity after 1931. The lens was made in Paris by a famous workshop (it weighed almost two tonnes) and it floated on a bath of mercury so that it could turn smoothly.

The keepers kept spare wicks, spare glass and spare oil in a store at the foot of the tower. A small boat brought fresh supplies every second week, weather permitting, and the keepers signalled with flags when they needed help.
